label: 1986 conference transcription: reported torsion displacement

label: Kozlov 2009 on Euler's Petersburg work and Russian impact
normalized_summary: Euler arrived in St. Petersburg in 1727, worked at the St. Petersburg Academy during two major periods, and his works gave a major impetus to mathematics especially in Russia.

label: Kozlov 2009 on Chebyshev editing Euler and founding Petersburg school
normalized_summary: Kozlov identifies Chebyshev as founder of the St. Petersburg mathematical school and states that, as a young mathematician, Chebyshev actively edited and published Euler's works, which strongly stimulated his own investigations.

label: Kozlov 2009 on Markov and Lyapunov as Chebyshev students
normalized_summary: The article identifies A. A. Markov and A. M. Lyapunov among Chebyshev's students and as significant contributors to mathematics within the Academy of Sciences.

label: 2007 Russian historical transcription of Lyapunov general stability system
locator: MathNet indexed text, discussion of General Problem of Stability of Motion
normalized_summary: The historical article writes Lyapunov's general stability problem as dx_k/dt = X_k, k=1,...,n, with X_k functions of t and the state variables.

label: Tikhonov 1963 Fredholm first-kind forward equation
normalized_summary: A[x,z(s)] = integral_a^b K(x,s) z(s) ds = u(x), c <= x <= d.

label: Tikhonov 1963 definition of regularized family
normalized_summary: A family z^alpha(s) is called a regularized family of approximate solutions when A[x,z^alpha] tends to u as alpha tends to zero and each z^alpha belongs to a compact class containing the desired solution.

label: Tikhonov 1963 smoothing functional equation (2)
normalized_summary: M^alpha[z,u_bar] = N[z,u_bar] + alpha Omega[z].

label: Tikhonov 1963 data-misfit and smoothing terms
locator: Primary scan p. 502, definitions immediately below equation (2)
normalized_summary: N is the squared data mismatch integral and Omega is the integral of k(s)(z'(s))^2 + p(s)z(s)^2 with k(s)>0 and p(s)>0.

label: Vlasov reproduction on long-range collective interaction
normalized_summary: Vlasov argues that collision-only kinetic treatment is insufficient for charged-particle systems and that interactions over distances larger than the mean interparticle spacing play an essential role.

label: Vlasov reproduction linearized continuity-motion-field system (A)
normalized_summary: Linearized continuity, motion, and electrostatic field equations for small electron-density perturbations.

label: Vlasov reproduction plasma oscillator equation
normalized_summary: Eliminating E1 and u1 gives d^2 rho1/dt^2 + omega0^2 rho1 = 0 with omega0^2 = 4 pi N e^2 / m.

label: Vlasov reproduction self-consistent kinetic-Maxwell system (I)
normalized_summary: Distribution functions evolve under transport, Lorentz-force field terms and collision terms, while Maxwell equations use charge/current integrals of the same distribution functions.

label: Chebyshev 1853 finite-interval minimax approximation objective
normalized_summary: Chebyshev distinguishes local Taylor approximation from choosing a degree-n polynomial whose maximum deviation from f(x) over a finite interval is smaller than that of every other polynomial of the same degree; he then states the equal-extrema condition with at least n+2 extrema of equal numerical magnitude.

label: Chebyshev 1853 minimax extremal equation (1)
normalized_summary: (f(x)-U(x))^2 - L^2 = 0 has the n+2 extremal roots used to determine the polynomial coefficients and common extremal magnitude L.

label: Chebyshev 1853 endpoint/extremum equation (2)
normalized_summary: (x-a+h)(x-a-h) d(f(x)-U(x))/dx = 0 encodes interior stationary extrema together with the two interval endpoints.

label: Chebyshev 1853 normalization of finite interval
locator: Facsimile p. 543; OCR lines corresponding to x-a=hz
normalized_summary: Chebyshev substitutes x-a = h z, mapping x in [a-h,a+h] to z in [-1,1], and writes the approximation error in the normalized variable.

label: Pontryagin 1960 controlled state equation (1)
locator: Primary PDF pp. 4–5, equation (1); extracted PDF lines 88–95
normalized_summary: The object's motion is governed by dx^i/dt=f^i(x,u), i=1,...,n, with controls u in the control region U.

label: Pontryagin 1960 objective functional (4)
locator: Primary PDF p. 5, equation (4); extracted PDF lines 127–132
normalized_summary: Among admissible controls transferring x0 to x1, minimize J=integral from t0 to t1 of f^0(x(t),u(t)) dt.

label: Pontryagin 1960 Hamiltonian and canonical system
locator: Primary article p. 11; equations (18),(19), cross-checked against full-text mirror
normalized_summary: For the time-optimal specialization, H(psi,x,u)=sum_i psi_i f^i(x,u), and the state/adjoint equations are dx^i/dt=partial H/partial psi_i and dpsi_i/dt=-partial H/partial x^i.

label: Pontryagin 1960 maximum condition (20)
locator: Primary article p. 11, equation (20), full-text extraction
normalized_summary: For almost all t, H(psi(t),x(t),u(t)) equals M(psi(t),x(t)), where M is the supremum of H over u in U.
